diagnostic_evidence.quote:
\dot r_u^\theta(\tau)
        =
    \hat r_R \big( 1 -  r_u^\theta(\tau) \big) r_u^\theta(\tau) - \hat d_T r_u^\theta(\tau)

issues.failure_explanation: For positive r, the sign changes where \hat r_R(1-r)-\hat d_T=0, namely at r=1-\hat d_T/\hat r_R when this lies in [0,1], not at \hat r_R/(\hat r_R+\hat d_T). For example, \hat r_R=1 and \hat d_T=1/2 give a sign change at 1/2, while the proof claims nonnegative derivative through 2/3. The displayed threshold is also undefined when both parameters vanish. Thus the inference used to declare this boundary segment invariant is false as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the erroneous sign split by the direct boundary argument: r=0 is invariant because the equation has a factor r, and at r=1 the derivative is -\hat d_T\leq0. Together with the other boundary checks, this proves invariance without dividing by parameters.
issues.overall_effect: The supplied proof of simplex invariance is invalid at this step, so results using invariance to replace the original fields by truncated fields or to identify the original and extended objectives are not fully established by the written argument.
issues.title: Incorrect sign analysis on an invariant boundary
issues.why_classification: A short local boundary calculation repairs the proof for all nonnegative parameter values without changing the lemma, any dependent result, or the paper's scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: we discretized the interval $[0.5,1]$ where $\hat r_R$ varies into $25$ equi\-spaced nodes with distance $0.02$. Hence, we set $U(0.5,1)\approx \frac{1}{25}\sum_{j=1}^{25} \delta_{\hat r_R^j}$, with $\hat r_R^j\in \{0.5, 0.52,\ldots,1\}$.
which has a support consisting of $N=1225$ points.

issues.failure_explanation: The inclusive arithmetic progression 0.5,0.52,...,1 contains 26 nodes, since it has 25 intervals of length 0.02. It therefore cannot simultaneously be the stated 25-node set used with weights 1/25 and produce 25\times49=1225 tumors. The source does not determine whether the endpoint 1 was omitted, the spacing was different, or 26 nodes and different weights were actually used.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose and state one consistent grid—either 25 nodes with corrected spacing or endpoint convention, or all 26 listed nodes with weights 1/26—and rerun the optimizations and all ensemble statistics using that grid.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete ensemble used for every numerical objective, optimization, benchmark average, and performance table is not uniquely specified, so the reported simulations cannot be reproduced from the stated construction.
issues.title: The stated parameter grid has 26 resistant-growth nodes, not 25
issues.why_classification: The conceptual method survives, but resolving the ambiguity requires selecting a different discrete measure and recomputing the numerical optimizers, tables, and comparisons rather than making a purely textual correction.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
However, in the first part of the treatment, the total tumor size exceeds the progression threshold.
Hence, it turns out that for such a strategy $\tau_{TTP}^\theta < \tau_{TTP'}^\theta$
\caption{\footnotesize Comparison in terms of Time-to-Progression (TTP) between the schedules obtained by minimizing $\J^1$ (linear) and $\J^2$ (hyperbolic).

issues.failure_explanation: TTP is expressly defined as the first threshold crossing, whereas TTP-prime is the last time at or below the threshold. The paper acknowledges that the hyperbolic trajectories cross the progression threshold early and later return below it, so TTP-prime is strictly larger and measures a different event. Substituting it only for the hyperbolic policy is not a fair TTP comparison and does not support claims that this policy improves Time-to-Progression over MTD or adaptive therapy.

failure_location.quote: We insist on the fact that for having a fair evaluation of the TTP, in the rows marked as `Hyperbolic' (corresponding to the cost $\ell^2$), we used $\tau_{TTP'}^\theta$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Relabel and interpret all hyperbolic results as TTP-prime and withdraw comparisons to benchmark TTP values unless those benchmarks are also evaluated under the same metric. To retain genuine TTP claims, recompute and compare the first-crossing times for every strategy.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised TTP improvements for the hyperbolic policy, including the corresponding table interpretation and the introduction's claim of outperforming MTD and AT in TTP, are unsupported. The reported numbers can only be interpreted as values of the distinct TTP-prime metric.
issues.title: Post-recovery TTP-prime is reported as Time-to-Progression
issues.why_classification: A consistent relabeling preserves numerical values but abandons the central claimed guarantee of improved Time-to-Progression; retaining that guarantee requires materially different evaluations and may reverse the conclusions.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Namely, we aim to formulate an adaptive therapy that allows tumor growth to be controlled at the early stage of the therapy, without exceeding the progression threshold.
However, as soon as the tumor size gets close to the progression threshold, the therapy is started.

issues.failure_explanation: Under the paper's definition, progression occurs at the first instant the tumor reaches or exceeds 1.2n_0. Step 1 deliberately keeps treatment off until precisely that event, and Step 2 reacts only after observing it. Thus the procedure cannot ensure that the initial growth remains short of progression, contrary to its stated design rationale; with discrete monitoring it may also overshoot the threshold before treatment begins.

failure_location.quote:
\item At $\tau =0$, set {$u=0$} and keep it constant while $s^\theta(\tau) + r^\theta(\tau)<  1.2\, n_0$ (vacation period).
\item After observing $s^\theta(\tau)+r^\theta(\tau)\geq 1.2\, n_0$, reset {$u=1$}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must introduce a treatment trigger strictly below 1.2n_0, account for observation or discretization delay, and rerun the simulations to determine whether the claimed TTP improvements remain.
issues.overall_effect: The Off-On construction does not provide the claimed early control without progression, and its table cannot represent delayed first-crossing TTP values without an unstated change of metric. Consequently, the asserted TTP advantage of Off-On therapy is not established by the stated procedure.
issues.title: Off-On therapy initiates treatment only after progression has occurred
issues.why_classification: The current switching rule is structurally incompatible with the claimed no-progression objective. The source supplies no lower trigger or analysis showing that a redesigned rule retains comparable performance, so preserving the guarantee requires a new algorithmic choice and new numerical validation.
